self_critique:
Run critique

What was suboptimal
- The search was very shallow: only two successful improvements and one failed proposal before declaring convergence. That is insufficient evidence that the modeling space was exhausted.
- Acceptance appears too permissive. Gains were roughly +0.0014 at each step, while the reported sigma=0.0001 is only shown for the baseline and may not capture seed, split, or validation-selection variance. Repeated selection on one validation set can easily overstate gains of this size.
- Node_001 predicted at least +0.002 but delivered about +0.0014. It was still useful, but the hypothesis was not calibrated and the run did not record ablations showing which add-ons contributed.
- Node_002 failed without a preserved proposal, error classification, or recovery attempt. That loses information and makes the lineage opaque. Node_003 being shown as a child of a failed node is also semantically awkward; it should branch from the last valid checkpoint.
- The final gain came from a five-seed rank ensemble. This is a reasonable variance-reduction tactic, but it multiplies inference/training cost and does not establish that the underlying model improved. No single-seed matched-cost comparison or ensemble-size curve was reported.
- The policy focused on incremental validation tuning around one champion. It did not explore genuinely diverse model families, split robustness, calibration, or error slices.

Scaffold changes
- Require multi-seed estimates and confidence intervals for small gains; use paired per-example bootstrap or repeated splits where feasible.
- Separate “single-model quality” from “ensemble quality,” and report compute/storage/latency costs.
- Add mandatory ablations for bundled feature/objective proposals. Node_001 combined several add-ons, so its causal value is unclear.
- Preserve failed proposals, stack traces, failure categories, and attempted repairs. Resume from the last successful node.
- Add a validation-budget rule or nested holdout to limit adaptive overfitting.
- Do not declare convergence after so few trials. Require either a minimum breadth of distinct hypotheses or several consecutive well-powered failures.
- Record exact metrics rather than rounded values, along with secondary metrics and slice-level effects.

What the next run should try first
1. Re-evaluate node_001 across multiple seeds and, ideally, a fresh validation split. Confirm that its approximately +0.0014 gain is real.
2. Run one-at-a-time and leave-one-out ablations for ordinal watch ratio, duration regime, CWM censoring, and recency features.
3. Build an ensemble-size curve for 1/2/3/5 seeds and compare rank averaging with probability/logit averaging. Select the smallest ensemble that retains most of the gain.
4. If the gain survives, seek diversity rather than more identical seeds: blend the DCN-lite model with a materially different architecture or objective and measure residual/ranking-error complementarity.

The highest-priority next action is robust multi-seed confirmation plus ablation of node_001 before further optimizing the five-seed ensemble.
